description:
Set text content on one or more TEXT nodes. For whole-node styling (font, size, weight, color), use edit.

The text parser supports mixed inline styles in the same existing TEXT node:

- `**bold**`, `*italic*`, `***bold italic***`, and `~~strikethrough~~`
- `{color:#EF4444|red text}` and `{size:20|large text}`
- nesting such as `{color:#EF4444|**$9**}`

Use `set_text` or `edit` content for brace spans on existing nodes. The parser removes the markup and applies Figma range styles; do not split one sentence into multiple text nodes.
When the user identifies an exact phrase, put that phrase literally inside the markup in the tool argument—for example `{color:#EF4444|**annual plan**}`. Do not replace the executable syntax with prose such as “apply nested bold and red markup.”

Use when:
- Changing what a TEXT node says — labels, titles, button text, body copy
- Batch-updating multiple text nodes in one call
- Applying mixed inline emphasis while replacing the node's content

Returns: { data: { id, name, type, applied?, noop?, rejected? } } (Batch: { data: { count, results, errors?, partial? } }).
`applied`/`noop` list prop keys; `rejected: [{key, reason}]` is TERMINAL (prop invalid for this node type / readonly) — do not retry it. If the only requested prop is rejected, returns `{ error }`.

`partial: true` means some entries succeeded and some failed — check `errors[]` for which entries to retry.

Skip when:
- You want to change font/size/weight — use edit({node, props: {fontFamily, fontSize, ...}})
- You want to bind text to a STRING variable — use bind_variable

Line truncation is a node property, not content. Use `edit` with a bounded width and `maxLines`; an unbounded text node cannot clamp reliably.

Examples:
```text
set_text({node: "1:2", text: "Sign in"})
set_text({node: "1:2", text: "Now {color:#EF4444|**$9**}"})
set_text({nodes: [{node: "1:2", text: "A"}, {node: "1:3", text: "B"}]})
```
